comment: What must not silently disappear from shipreport. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces; `split` declares which half of the skill is deterministic; `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run.

prose.pattern: Every claim in the report carries a receipt — a commit SHA,
prose.rationale: The one rule. It is the reason this skill exists rather than a prompt; lose the line and the skill becomes a generic assistant with extra steps.

prose.pattern: Never claim a result you did not observe
prose.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

prose.pattern: never ask about anything in it
prose.rationale: Two questions maximum is only achievable because detection already answered the rest. Asking about a detectable signal is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form.

prose.pattern: A generic icon is a failure
prose.rationale: The card scenes are the reason the sheet is worth looking at. The moment a run reaches for a stock glyph the report becomes a list with decoration, and nothing in code can tell the difference between a lazy drawing and a considered one.

prose.pattern: Never shell out for something the corpus holds
prose.rationale: The first real run read its releases with three networked `gh` loops and printed sixteen kilobytes of changelog into the conversation, in a skill whose own presentation contract forbids exactly that. `show` exists so step 4 costs no network and no wall of text; the moment a run reaches for `gh` again, both come back.

prose.pattern: the fix for that is a fix to the checker with a test on both sides
prose.rationale: The gate once called the phrase "plus/minus" a repository name and the run reworded a true sentence to satisfy it. "Never weaken the gate" must not become "always believe the gate": a false positive teaches a run that the gate is an obstacle to be worded around, which is how a gate stops being believed at all.

deterministic.step: collect GitHub contributions and Claude session transcripts, redact secrets and absolute paths at ingest so nothing unsafe is ever cached, and record a watermark so the second run is cheap
score and order every candidate in the requested window, draw the line between what appears in the report and what does not, and say when that line was a tiebreak rather than a ranking
read the artifact behind a receipt — a release's changelog, a pull request's body, a session's shape — from the corpus rather than from the network
resolve every citation in the drafted report back to a real artifact, failing the run when one does not resolve
render the ranked items and approved prose into the press-styled HTML report

nondeterministic.step: merge several ranked items into the one outcome a stakeholder would recognise, and choose the headline the time frame was actually about
nondeterministic.why: the score orders candidates but cannot tell that three pull requests were one piece of work, and nothing on disk records which of them a reader would care about

nondeterministic.step: write the prose for a reader with no context on the code — plain outcomes, no repository names or commit hashes in the body
nondeterministic.why: translating a diff into why it mattered is judgment, and the audience is a person who was not there

nondeterministic.step: decide what an ambiguous session actually accomplished when its commits and its transcript disagree
nondeterministic.why: a session that ends without a commit may have been abandoned or may have been the investigation that made the next day cheap, and only a reader of the transcript can tell

_baseline_comment: Pinned against a real run of this skill, never a synthetic fixture. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, so CI cannot spend and cannot flake.

baseline.rationale: the ranking silently reordering or dropping an item while still producing a complete-looking report, and the rendered report losing a section or its receipt appendix — pinned against a real run over a frozen corpus — this machine's own Claude session transcripts and real GitHub contribution output for a real week, with rank and render re-run and byte-compared.

the receipts gate weakening until a claim with no artifact behind it reaches the report, which is the one rule failing silently — pinned against a drafted report carrying one citation that names a commit not present in the corpus.

redaction being moved, weakened or skipped so that a secret is written to the on-disk corpus, where every later run and every model pass would read it — pinned against a real transcript fixture seeded with a token-shaped string and an absolute home path.

the four defects a real run exposed on 2026-08-05 coming back — a ranking whose signals top out so twelve items tie and the line is drawn by a timestamp; the prose gate refusing English ("plus/minus" read as a repository) so a run learns to word around it; the art validator admitting a document-scoped <style>, a style-attribute colour or a script URL into the one field `render` splices unescaped; and GitHub items reaching the on-disk corpus without passing through redaction. Deliberately a separate file from baseline.test.mjs, which `skillfactory freeze` regenerates and would delete these guards from.

a resolver or glob matching nothing and reporting a clean empty run, so the golden passes while checking over zero items. The floor of 8 is the frozen artifact set itself — the two draft inputs, the frozen corpus, the manifest and the four re-run outputs; losing any one of them goes red. The floor on the corpus CONTENTS (549 contribution records, 124 session digests) is asserted in scripts/tests/units.test.mjs, which freeze does not regenerate.
